head: b7ee4555810dcb82b4a0714200c599ab076daac8
summary: Maintainers can authorize an agent to merge one verified commit when no required checks exist. Maintenance appears bounded, but consent handling for this exception lacks behavioral evidence; observed benefit and frequency remain unknown.
reasons: The change directly addresses #551: maintainers can authorize an agent to merge a verified commit without configuring required checks or clicking merge themselves. Actual time saved and incident frequency are unknown.
Scope remains bounded. One confirmation flag, result field, setup warning, and associated tests add ongoing maintenance without introducing dependencies or a new authorization system.
Reported fake-client tests cover exact-head confirmation and several refusals. They establish helper behavior, but do not exercise whether an agent supplies the flag only with valid Ask approval.

That distinction matters: eval/reports/ask-merge-authorization.md records an earlier unauthorized Ask merge caused by confusing general permission with approval. Its replay predates this exception. Reverting this PR cannot undo downstream merges, disclosures, or deployment effects.

The roughly 30 added workflow words describe a necessary authorization decision that Ruby cannot establish. SKILL.md loads the complete workflow for every delivery task, so all tasks carry that instruction cost. The packet omits actual bin/report-instruction-growth output, leaving rendered totals and other changed guidance unassessed.

Three local review rounds and CodeRabbit fixes show repair effort. The packet reports the substantive findings fixed and three remaining findings as nits; it identifies no earlier unresolved substantive finding.
concerns: skills/shaka/config/workflow.yml and enforcement.yml leave the new empty-checks exception dependent on agent judgment. No reported replay exercises approved Ask, unapproved Ask, Auto, resumed tasks, or changed-head approval with this flag. Given the documented authorization failure, this leaves a substantive risk of merging without valid consent.
alternative: Keep the bounded implementation and add a safe decision replay for the new exception, using the existing authorization evaluation approach. Include actual instruction-growth output and bind reported validation to the candidate. Live GitHub submission, empty-check queue behavior, and deployment effects remain unexercised; a replay can test consent without causing those effects.
next_action: Revise this PR's evidence with a safe authorization replay covering approved Ask, unapproved Ask, Auto, resumed tasks, and changed heads before recommending merge.
